chapters.1.lds: The selected lesson studies light and inviting others to come and see. Why does John direct his own followers toward another person?
chapters.1.summary: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God and was God. All things were made through him. The Word became flesh and lived among us. John the Baptist says he is not the Christ. He points to Jesus as the Lamb of God. Two of John’s disciples follow Jesus and spend the day with him. Andrew brings his brother Simon. Philip brings Nathanael, who doubts that anything good comes from Nazareth.
chapters.2.lds: The selected lesson studies the wedding sign and care for sacred places. How does later remembrance change the meaning of the temple saying?
chapters.2.summary: Jesus and his disciples attend a wedding at Cana. The wine runs out, and his mother tells him. He has six stone jars filled with water. The water becomes fine wine, and his disciples believe in him. He goes up to Jerusalem for the Passover. He drives the sellers and money changers out of the temple. He says, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking about his body.
chapters.3.lds: The selected lesson teaches spiritual rebirth through Christ. How does John’s bridegroom comparison answer his disciples’ concern about losing followers?
chapters.3.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes to Jesus at night. Jesus says no one can see God’s Kingdom without being born anew. Nicodemus asks how that can be. Jesus says God loved the world and gave his only Son. Light has come, and people loved darkness. John’s disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus. John says he is the bridegroom’s friend and is glad. He says Jesus must increase and he must decrease.
chapters.4.lds: The selected lesson reads living water through spiritual needs and growing testimony. How does the town’s own hearing develop the woman’s invitation?
chapters.4.summary: Jesus travels through Samaria and rests at Jacob’s well. He asks a Samaritan woman for a drink. He offers her living water and tells her about her life. She asks where people ought to worship. He says true worshipers worship in spirit and truth. She tells her town to come and see. Many Samaritans believe and ask him to stay. In Galilee he heals an official’s son with a word.
chapters.5.lds: Doctrine and Covenants 76:15–18 says a vision followed study of verse 29. What prevents the man from reaching the water before Jesus speaks?
chapters.5.summary: In Jerusalem many sick people lie beside a pool. One man has been ill for thirty-eight years. Jesus asks whether he wants to be well. The man says he has no one to put him in the water. Jesus tells him to take up his mat and walk. It is the Sabbath, and the leaders object. Jesus says his Father is working and he is working. He says the Scriptures testify about him.
chapters.6.lds: Why does Peter remain when other disciples leave after the same teaching?
chapters.6.summary: Jesus feeds five thousand with five barley loaves and two fish. The crowd wants to make him king, and he withdraws. He walks on the sea to his disciples. The crowd finds him and asks for more bread. He says he is the bread of life that came down from heaven. He speaks of eating his flesh and drinking his blood. Many disciples call this a hard saying and leave. Peter says there is no one else to go to.
chapters.7.lds: How does Nicodemus’ hearing request challenge the proposed judgment?
chapters.7.summary: Jesus’s brothers urge him to show himself at the Feast of Booths. He goes up in secret and then teaches in the temple. Some say he is a good man, and others say he deceives the people. Officers are sent to arrest him. On the last day he invites the thirsty to come and drink. The crowd is divided over him. The officers return without him and say no one ever spoke like this. Nicodemus asks whether the law judges a man unheard.
chapters.8.lds: How does claimed ancestry differ from the conduct Jesus names?
chapters.8.summary: Jesus says he is the light of the world. The Pharisees say his witness about himself is not valid. He tells those who believed him that the truth will set them free. They answer that they are Abraham’s children and were never slaves. He says everyone who sins is a slave to sin. If they were Abraham’s children, they would do what Abraham did. They are trying to kill him. He says, “Before Abraham came into existence, I AM.”
chapters.9.lds: What remains consistent in the man’s answers as the questions repeat?
chapters.9.summary: Jesus sees a man blind from birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it. He says neither, and he heals the man with mud and washing. Neighbors and Pharisees question the man again and again. His parents are afraid and say he can speak for himself. He says he knows one thing: he was blind and now sees. They throw him out. Jesus finds him, and the man worships him.
chapters.10.lds: In 3 Nephi 15:21 Jesus calls a Book of Mormon people his “other sheep.” What distinguishes the shepherd from the hired worker when danger comes?
chapters.10.summary: Jesus says the shepherd enters by the door and the sheep know his voice. A thief comes only to steal and kill. Jesus says he is the door and the good shepherd. A hired man runs when the wolf comes. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. He has other sheep that are not of this fold. At a winter feast some ask whether he is the Christ. He says, “I and the Father are one,” and they pick up stones.
chapters.11.lds: How does restored life become a reason for the council’s death plan?
chapters.11.summary: Lazarus of Bethany falls ill, and his sisters send for Jesus. Jesus arrives after Lazarus has been dead four days. Martha says she believes he is the Christ. Jesus weeps at the tomb. He calls Lazarus out, and the dead man comes out wrapped in cloths. Many believe, and some report it to the Pharisees. The council fears that Rome will destroy their place and nation. The high priest says one man should die for the people.
chapters.12.lds: How does the dying seed change expectations about the announced hour?
chapters.12.summary: Mary anoints Jesus’s feet with costly perfume, and Judas objects. A crowd welcomes Jesus to Jerusalem with palm branches. Some Greeks ask to see him. He says the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. A grain of wheat must fall into the earth and die to bear fruit. A voice from heaven answers him. He says that when he is lifted up he will draw all people to himself. Many still do not believe.
chapters.13.lds: Why does Jesus keep the titles Teacher and Lord while washing feet?
chapters.13.summary: Before the Passover Jesus rises from supper and ties a towel around himself. He washes his disciples’ feet. Peter objects and then asks to be washed all over. Jesus says they should wash one another’s feet. He is troubled and says one of them will betray him. Judas takes the bread and goes out into the night. Jesus gives a new commandment: love one another as he has loved them. He tells Peter that he will deny him three times.
chapters.14.lds: The selected lesson teaches the Holy Spirit’s help through teaching and remembrance. How will remembered words connect the promised Spirit with Jesus’ earlier teaching?
chapters.14.summary: Jesus tells his disciples not to be troubled. He is going to prepare a place for them. Thomas says they do not know the way. Jesus says he is the way, the truth, and the life. Philip asks to see the Father. Jesus says whoever has seen him has seen the Father. He promises another Counselor, the Spirit of truth. He leaves them his peace.
chapters.15.lds: The selected lesson connects remaining in Christ with fruit and joy. Why does the branch need to remain joined even when it already bears fruit?
chapters.15.summary: Jesus says he is the true vine and his Father is the gardener. Branches that bear fruit are pruned to bear more. A branch cannot bear fruit unless it remains in the vine. His disciples must remain in his love. His commandment is that they love one another as he loved them. He calls them friends and not servants. The world will hate them as it hated him. The Spirit and the disciples will bear witness.
chapters.16.lds: The selected lesson teaches guidance from the Holy Spirit. How does the scattering warning qualify the disciples’ new confidence?
chapters.16.summary: Jesus warns that his disciples will be put out of the synagogues. He says it is better for them that he goes away. The Counselor will come and guide them into all truth. They will weep, and their sorrow will turn to joy. He tells them to ask the Father in his name. The disciples say that now they understand and believe. He answers that they will soon be scattered and leave him alone. He tells them to take courage, for he has overcome the world.
chapters.17.lds: The selected lesson studies unity with the Father and among followers. Why does protection leave the followers within the world rather than remove them?
chapters.17.summary: Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and prays. He asks the Father to glorify the Son. He says eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ. He prays for those the Father gave him. He does not ask that they be taken out of the world. He asks that they be kept from the evil one. He prays also for those who will believe through their word. He asks that they all may be one.
chapters.18.lds: How does Jesus’ answer about fighting explain his kingdom to Pilate?
chapters.18.summary: Jesus goes to a garden across the Kidron, and Judas brings soldiers. Jesus steps forward and says, “I am he.” Peter cuts off a servant’s ear, and Jesus tells him to put away his sword. Jesus is taken to the high priest. Peter denies him three times by a fire. Jesus tells the high priest that he taught openly. He is brought to Pilate, who asks whether he is a king. Jesus says his Kingdom is not of this world.
chapters.19.lds: How does care for his mother stand beside the statement of completed work?
chapters.19.summary: Pilate has Jesus flogged, and soldiers crown him with thorns. Pilate says he finds no guilt and brings him out to the crowd. He hands him over to be crucified. The sign on the cross reads “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.” Soldiers divide his clothes. Jesus entrusts his mother to the disciple he loves. He says, “It is finished,” and dies. Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus bury him in a garden tomb.
chapters.20.lds: The selected lesson teaches resurrection through the Gospel accounts. How does the account’s stated purpose address readers who have not seen these signs?
chapters.20.summary: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb open and runs to Peter and another disciple. They see the grave cloths and go home. Mary stays weeping and meets Jesus, whom she takes for the gardener. He says her name, and she knows him. That evening he appears to the disciples behind locked doors. Thomas is absent and says he will not believe without touching the wounds. A week later Jesus invites him to touch. John says he wrote so that readers may believe.
chapters.21.lds: The selected lesson connects love for Christ with feeding his sheep. How does the final correction distinguish a conditional saying from a certain prediction?
chapters.21.summary: Seven disciples go fishing on the Sea of Tiberias and catch nothing. At dawn a man on the shore tells them to cast on the right side. The net fills, and they know it is the Lord. He gives them bread and fish beside a charcoal fire. He asks Peter three times whether he loves him. Each time he tells him to feed his sheep. Peter asks what will happen to another disciple. Jesus says that is not Peter’s concern.
